<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:MAPDEP_metric}
	Equation \eqref{eq:MAPDEP} shows that, after adopting the optimal MAP detector, the minimum detection error probability depends on the local quantizers only through the induced conditional distributions $p(\mathbf{u}|H_0)$ and $p(\mathbf{u}|H_1)$. Therefore, the detector need not be optimized separately, and $P_E(H,\mathbf{u})$ provides an exact finite-sensor objective for quantizer design.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:glob_opt_identical_quantizer}
	Suppose that the local observations are conditionally i.i.d. given $H$, and that all sensors are subject to the same $L$-level quantization constraint. \textcolor{black}{Assume that the local quantization randomizations are mutually independent across sensors and independent of $(H,X_1,\ldots,X_K)$. Then restricting all sensors to an identical quantizer does not change the supremum of the average network Chernoff information over all possibly heterogeneous local quantizers.} Specifically,
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:max_Chernoff}
		\begin{aligned}
			&\textcolor{black}{\sup_{\{p(u_k|X_k)\}_{k=1}^{K}}}C(H,\mathbf{u})=\\
			&\textcolor{black}{\sup_{p(u|X)}}\left\{-\min_{0\leq\lambda\leq 1}\log\left[\sum_{u=0}^{L-1}p(u|H_{0})^{\lambda}p(u|H_{1})^{1-\lambda}\right]\right\},
		\end{aligned}
	\end{equation}  
	where $p(u|H_i)=\mathbb{E}_{X|H_i}[p(u|X)],\ i=0,1$. In particular, if $p(u|X)^*$ attains the single-sensor \textcolor{black}{supremum} on the right-hand side of \eqref{eq:max_Chernoff}, deploying $p(u|X)^*$ at every sensor is globally optimal for maximizing the average network Chernoff information.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- ieeeproof-1: body_md -->
The proof is provided in Appendix~\ref{append:proof_identical_quantizer}.
<!-- end ieeeproof-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:MAPDEP_binary_quantize}
	If the binary quantized data $u_1,\ldots,u_K$ from all sensors are conditionally i.i.d. given $H$, then the MAPDEP under binary quantization is given by
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:MAPDEP_Binary_Quantization}
		\begin{aligned}
			P_E^{\text{Binary}}\triangleq\sum_{k=0}^{K}C_{K}^{k}\min&\left\{\pi_0(\gamma(H_0))^k(1-\gamma(H_0))^{K-k},\right.\\
			&\left.\pi_1(\gamma(H_1))^k(1-\gamma(H_1))^{K-k}\right\},
		\end{aligned}
	\end{equation}
	where 
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:binary_output_probability}
		\gamma(H)=P(u=1|H)=\mathbb{E}_{X|H}[p(u=1|X)],\ H\in\{H_0,H_1\},
	\end{equation}
		denotes the conditional probability that a quantized message equals `1' given $H$, and $C_K^k$ is the binomial coefficient.
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- ieeeproof-2: body_md -->
Please see Appendix~\ref{append:proof_MAPDEP_binary_quantize}.
<!-- end ieeeproof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{th:opt_mean_fusion}
	If the binary quantized data $u_k$, $k=1,\ldots,K$, from all sensors are conditionally i.i.d. given $H$, then detection using the quantized data $\mathbf{u}=[u_1,\dots,u_K]^T$ or their average $\bar{u} = \frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K} u_k$ achieves the same minimum detection error probability, i.e.,
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:mean_fusion_MAPDEP}
		\begin{aligned}
			P_{E}(H,\mathbf{u})=&P_E^{\text{Binary}}\\
			=&P_{E}(H,\bar{u})\triangleq\sum_{\bar{u}}\min\left\{\pi_0p(\bar{u}|H_0),\pi_1p(\bar{u}|H_1)\right\},
		\end{aligned}
	\end{equation}
		where $P_{E}(H,\bar{u})$ is the minimum detection error probability achieved by using $\bar{u}$ to detect $H$.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- ieeeproof-3: body_md -->
Please see Appendix~\ref{append:proof_mean_fusion}.
<!-- end ieeeproof-3 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:tree_distribution}
	Given an observation $X$, suppose the binary codeword $\mathbf b=[b_1,\dots,b_M]^T$ is generated according to the sequential dithering procedure. Denote the induced distribution of this random output by $P_{\mathrm{SD}}(\cdot\mid X)$. Then, for any level $u_l\in\mathcal U$ with associated codeword $\mathbf b^{(l)}=[b_1^{(l)},\dots,b_M^{(l)}]^T$ and induced internal-node sequence $\{v_0^{(l)},v_1^{(l)},\dots,v_{M-1}^{(l)}\}$ defined by \eqref{eq:traversal_rule}, we have
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:prop_level}
		P_{\mathrm{SD}}(u=u_l\mid X) = [\mathbf q(X)]_l,
	\end{equation}
	where $[\mathbf q(X)]_l$ is the model-induced probability defined in \eqref{eq:codeword_prob}.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- ieeeproof-4: body_md -->
The proof is provided in Appendix~\ref{append:proof_tree_distribution}.
<!-- end ieeeproof-4 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:multibit_surrogate_scope}
	Equation \eqref{eq:multibit_loss} provides a computationally tractable Bhattacharyya design objective whose evaluation is linear in the number of quantization levels. Its optimized Chernoff counterpart characterizes the asymptotic Bayesian error exponent, and \eqref{eq:multibit_loss} attains the same exponent when $\lambda^*=1/2$. At finite $K$, it serves as an upper-bound surrogate rather than the exact MAP error.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{th:multibit_mean_fusion}
	If the $M$-bit quantized data from all sensors are conditionally i.i.d. given $H$, then detection using the full quantized data, i.e., the collection of binary codewords $\mathbf{B}=[\mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2,\ldots,\mathbf{b}_K]^T$, or their mean one-hot vector $\bar{\mathbf{v}}=\frac{1}{K}\sum_{k=1}^{K}\mathbf{v}_k$ achieves the same minimum detection error probability, i.e.,
	\begin{equation}\label{eq:multi_bit_error_prob}
		\begin{aligned}
			P_E\left(H, \mathbf{B}\right) & = P_E\left(H, \bar{\mathbf{v}}\right)\\
			& = \sum_{\bar{\mathbf{v}}}\min\left\{\pi_0p(\bar{\mathbf{v}} | H_0), \pi_1p(\bar{\mathbf{v}} | H_1)\right\}.
		\end{aligned}
	\end{equation}
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- ieeeproof-5: body_md -->
The proof is provided in Appendix~\ref{append:th_multibit_mean_fusion}.
<!-- end ieeeproof-5 -->
